title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: One click, not one per file
summary: The bulk commands ask once now, up front: apply all, or review one by one. The Refactor Preview has no select all, so 171 changes over 43 files meant 43 clicks.

highlights.title: Apply all, or review one by one
highlights.description: The flag that opens the Refactor Preview is the same one that leaves every box unticked. Asking once, before the edit is built, replaces a click per file with a single answer for the lot.

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: Four bulk commands ask once instead of once per file: narrow every self only member, remove code used only by tests, clean dead code across the workspace, and remove unread Remote Config keys.
The cascade that trails a removal follows what the command decided rather than asking again on its own.

sections.heading: Notes
bullets: The dialog counts the changes and the files before anything happens, and closing it applies nothing.
The VS Code test double threw away the metadata that carries this flag, so half the behaviour could not be asserted. It keeps it now, and both modes are pinned by a test.
